= Links and Images

A link macro gets its text from the brackets:

link:https://example.com/docs[the documentation]

Empty brackets make the link show its target:

link:https://example.com[]

A bare URL becomes a link where it appears.

Sentence punctuation after the URL is not part of the link:

https://example.com/a/b.

Punctuation inside a URL stays in the URL when more URL text follows it:

https://sub.example.com/a.html

Underscores inside a URL stay in the URL too:

https://example.com/a_b_c

An inline image sits inside a line of text:

This line has image:icon.png[icon] in it.

A block image stands alone on its line:

image::photo.jpg[A scenic photo]

Alt text is optional.

The renderer still writes the `alt` attribute:

image::diagram.svg[]
